title: How to Grill Sliced Watermelon for a Unique Summer Side
meta_description: Elevate your summer BBQ with grilled watermelon! Learn how to grill watermelon on grill mat for perfect sear marks without the sticky mess or flare-ups.
html:
Most people think of watermelon as a refreshing, cold platter on the picnic table. But if you’ve never tried it hot, you’re missing out on a serious flavor upgrade. Grilling watermelon caramelizes the natural sugars, transforming the texture from watery and crisp to dense and steak-like, with a smoky finish that pairs perfectly with salty feta or spicy chili flakes.

The challenge with grilling fruit is that it's delicate. Watermelon can easily slip through the grates or stick and tear when you try to flip it. That is why I always grill watermelon on grill mat. Using BBQ Grill Mats allows you to get those beautiful char marks and a deep sear without the fruit falling apart or causing messy flare-ups from dripping sugars.

The Best Watermelon for the Grill

Not all watermelons are created equal when it comes to heat. For grilling, you want a melon that is ripe but still firm. If the watermelon is overripe, it becomes too soft and will essentially collapse into a mushy pile on the grill.

I recommend seedless varieties for the best eating experience. When slicing, aim for thick rounds or wedges about 1 to 1.5 inches thick. If the slices are too thin, they’ll cook through too quickly and lose that satisfying contrast between the charred exterior and the juicy center.

How to Grill Watermelon on Grill Mat for Best Results

The secret to a perfect grilled slice is high heat and a non-stick surface. Because watermelon has a high water content, it doesn't "brown" as quickly as a steak; it needs a quick, intense sear.

Start by preheating your grill to medium-high. Place your BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grates. The mat creates a protective barrier that prevents the fruit from sticking to the metal and keeps the heat evenly distributed. This is especially helpful if you are using a charcoal grill where hot spots are common.

Brush both sides of your watermelon slices with a neutral oil (like avocado or grapeseed) or a bit of melted butter. Place the slices on the mat and leave them alone for 3 to 5 minutes. Resist the urge to move them; you want the sugars to caramelize and create a crust. Flip carefully and grill for another 3 to 5 minutes.

Flavor Pairings to Level Up Your Side Dish

While grilled watermelon is great on its own, it really shines when you play with the balance of sweet, salty, and acidic flavors. Since the grilling process intensifies the sweetness, you need a counterpoint.

  • The Mediterranean Mix: Top your warm slices with crumbled feta cheese, fresh mint leaves, and a squeeze of lime juice.
  • The Spicy Kick: Dust the slices with Tajín or a mix of chili powder and sea salt immediately after removing them from the heat.
  • The Balsamic Glaze: Drizzle a thick balsamic reduction over the slices and garnish with a few cracks of black pepper.
  • The Herbaceous Touch: Use a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of fresh basil or cilantro.

Cleaning Up After Grilling Fruit

One of the biggest headaches of grilling fruit is the sticky residue left behind. When sugar drips onto hot grates, it carbonizes and creates a stubborn crust that requires heavy scrubbing. This is another reason why I prefer to grill watermelon on grill mat.

Instead of scrubbing your grill grates for twenty minutes, you simply remove the BBQ Grill Mats once they've cooled. Most of the residue stays on the mat, which can be wiped down or washed with soapy water. It keeps your grill clean for the next meal and saves you a ton of effort during the cleanup phase of your summer party.

Pro Tips for the Perfect Sear

If you find your watermelon is releasing too much moisture, don't panic. This is normal. The mat will keep the slices from sinking into that liquid, ensuring you get a sear rather than a steam. For an even deeper flavor, try marinating the slices in a mixture of lime juice and honey for 15 minutes before they hit the grill.

Remember that timing is everything. You aren't trying to "cook" the watermelon in the traditional sense—you're just searing the outside. As soon as you see those dark, caramelized grill lines, get them off the heat and onto the serving platter.

FAQ

Do I need to peel the watermelon before grilling?

Yes, you should remove the green rind entirely. However, leaving a tiny bit of the white pith can help the slice hold its shape better on the grill.

Can I use a grill mat on a gas grill?

Absolutely. BBQ Grill Mats are designed to work on gas, charcoal, and pellet grills. They are a great way to prevent flare-ups on gas grills when cooking sugary foods.

Will the watermelon taste like the grill?

Yes, it picks up a subtle, smoky aroma that complements the sweetness. Using a mat ensures you get that grilled flavor without the fruit sticking or burning in uneven patches.
